body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The Arvin City Council's vote to file a formal complaint against its former interim city attorney over alleged overbilling leads our news this morning, and Kern County supervisors spent Tuesday in a sharp argument over whether county dollars should help people released from ICE custody get home. Outside, it's a mild fall day — a high near 70, moderate air quality, and no weather alerts anywhere in the county.

## The Kern Overnight

The most serious call of the night came at 9:32 p.m., when officers were sent near Wible Road for a man in a tan shirt and black pants armed with a knife, reported to be trying to stab someone. Medical units staged nearby in case they were needed.

In north Bakersfield, officers were sent to a home on Wainwright Drive at 1:52 a.m. for a woman in her late 30s, known to carry a knife, who was trying to climb through a window. Two domestic violence calls came in during the evening: one at 9:13 p.m. at an apartment in the 9200 block of California Avenue, where two juveniles were inside and the address had a history of domestic violence, and another at 11:25 p.m. in the 5000 block of Pierce Road, where the man left on a red and black scooter.

A person listed as at risk left a home in the 2600 block of Cherry Street in central Bakersfield on foot at about 6 p.m. after a disturbance, saying he wanted to die. He was last seen in a burgundy or black sweatshirt and dark shoes, and was still missing as of the overnight report.

The night's heaviest fire came at 2:08 a.m., with heavy fire from the rear of a structure that crews could not reach with an attack line. Battalion 1 took command, a truck was asked to ventilate the building, and building utilities and the gas company were notified. Earlier, at 7:04 p.m., a full structure response went to the 800 block of Piute Street in southwest Bakersfield for a gas leak inside a home with a fire detector sounding. A rescue crew was sent outside the rescue mission on East 21st Street at 7:05 p.m. for a person close to fainting, and at 7:11 p.m. an adult woman was reported hurt in the 1700 block of South Chester Avenue near a gas station; her boyfriend took her for care in a private vehicle and the ambulance was not needed.

## Today's weather

It's 52 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 70 and a low around 53 tonight — an easy, classic late-October day in the valley. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires to report. Air quality sits at 67, which is moderate, so most people can be outside without worry, though those who are sensitive to particulates may want to keep an eye on it if they're planning a long stretch of exertion. Light layers this morning, short sleeves by afternoon.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that the Arvin City Council voted to file a formal complaint against its former interim city attorney, Nathan Hodges, over allegations that his law office overcharged the city.** The vote was four in favor with one abstention — Council member Donny Horton — and sends the complaint to the State Bar of California, where the Office of Chief Trial Counsel will review it. The complaint alleges Hodges violated rules of professional conduct during his time as the city's interim city attorney. The issue grew out of a Kern County Grand Jury report that flagged discrepancies in attorney fees during Hodges' tenure and advised the city to dig deeper, while noting the city shares responsibility because the mayor signs off on all invoices. Arvin later hired an outside consulting firm, which says it found overbilling across the invoices it examined. The council had previously met in closed session and asked current City Attorney Stephanie Gutierrez to prepare the complaint and try to recoup nearly $79,000. After Tuesday's meeting, Mayor Olivia Calderon said the city brought the matter forward to be a good steward of the community.

**According to 23ABC, Kern County supervisors argued openly Tuesday over a proposal to spend up to $50,000 in county funds helping people released from ICE custody return to their home communities, then voted unanimously to send the measure to committee without approving any spending.** County staff told the board that some people released from custody arrive without phones, identification or money and need help arranging travel. The money would have flowed through a county-contracted service provider to cover transportation, overnight lodging and meals, including travel to destinations outside California. Supervisors Jeff Flores and Leticia Perez clashed sharply over whether tax dollars should cover the cost, with Perez calling Flores "a coward" from the dais. Jeannie Parent, coordinator for Kern Welcoming and Extending Solidarity to Immigrants, told the board that community groups currently rely on donations for that help, describing people who are simply pointed toward the bus station without their belongings or a phone. The board directed the Finance and Administration Committee to determine whether a gap in services exists and who, if anyone, should pay to fill it.

**KGET 17 reports that Kern County District Attorney Zimmer has responded to recall efforts against him, calling them "organized by criminals."** The station's headline does not include further detail on the response or on the recall campaign itself.

**KGET 17 also reports that Kern County supervisors will consider a new recommendation concerning a decertified former deputy's possible new role with the District Attorney's office.** No further details were available from the headline alone.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Kern County voters are citing gas prices among their top concerns ahead of the midterm elections.** The station's headline does not include additional detail on the polling or the voters surveyed.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a MiG-29 made a landing at Meadows Field Airport in Bakersfield following a report of hot brakes.** The headline did not include further information on the aircraft or the outcome.

## Something good

There's new green space to enjoy north of the river. The North of the River Parks District and Lennar, the homebuilder behind the Gossamer Grove and Marcona Preserve communities, celebrated the opening of two new parks at Marcona Preserve. Together they span 2.75 acres and include putting greens, chess tables, a ping-pong table and cornhole. Lennar says the parks are meant to be places where neighbors connect and families make memories, and with the addition, North of the River now counts 27 parks in its district.

## Coming up this week

The Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. Elias Medina takes the stage Friday, October 30, followed by Journey USA on Saturday, November 7, sharing the date with Texas Tornado Tradition. The Cults & Classics series continues with "Play Misty for Me" on Monday, November 9, and NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives Friday, November 13. Season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are also on sale.

On the civic side, Bakersfield's City Council meets Wednesday, November 4, with a 3:30 p.m. session and a 5:15 p.m. session on the calendar — two chances that day to weigh in or just listen in on what the council is taking up. If you've been meaning to pay closer attention to local decisions, that's the week to do it.

Have a good Wednesday, Bakersfield.

top.title: Arvin City Council votes to file formal complaint against former city attorney
